description: Sample shared order inbox for the DeliveryLens Order desk. Synthetic emails from real client ids in data/halcyon-dataset/clients.csv whose primary_order_channel is Email. Dates are in late October 2026; header times are US Central (the warehouse time zone).

messages.what_it_demonstrates: A clean email from an at-risk client goes straight to the pick list with no typing. The old spreadsheet would send it with Carrier F, which is weak to the Northeast.
Cause 2 (incomplete address): the order is held before picking and a follow-up asking for the postcode is drafted, instead of shipping and failing at the door.
Cause 2 again with a different layout: only a city, state and ZIP are given, so the street is requested.
Cause 3 (same-day after the 08:00 cutoff): the order is accepted but honestly re-promised as next-day, because today's pick list is already printed.
A same-day order before 08:00 makes today's pick list and keeps its same-day promise.
The intake agent reads an address written on one line, which a fixed template cannot.
A different client layout (a text table with several lines) is read without a template for it.

messages.scenario: West destination, nearest warehouse out of stock
messages.what_it_demonstrates: Cause 4 (stock not at the nearest warehouse): W5 West has no HX-4410, so the order ships from a Midwest warehouse about 1,500 miles away, and the agent warns about it.
Cause 1 (weak carrier lane): the old spreadsheet picks Carrier F, the cheapest, which is about 53% on time to the Southeast; the advisor picks a strong carrier for this at-risk client.
The guardrail stops an email that tries to give the AI instructions; nothing reaches the model or the warehouse system.
"A couple of pallets of the usual" has no SKU or number, so the agent does not guess: it routes the order to a person.

messages.scenario: Order lines in an attached CSV purchase order
messages.what_it_demonstrates: The order lines are only in the CSV attachment; the agent reads the attachment as well as the email body.
